tasks.short: Plan forklift, VCA and food safety sessions around rooms, trainers, forklifts and shift rosters on three sites.

today.trigger: Studytube certificate expiry list, new hires or flex intake, or a manager asking for a session.
steps: Pull expiring certificates and open enrolments from Studytube into Excel
Check trainer and room availability in Outlook calendars and with external providers
Check shift rosters with site supervisors so warehouse staff can attend
Book the session in Studytube and send Outlook invites
Rebook when people drop out or a trainer cancels
drudgery: Cross-checking expiry lists against rosters by hand
Chasing supervisors for who can be released
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth with site supervisors and providers on dates, and rebooking after drop-outs in peak season.

lenses.faster: A scheduler reads expiries, rosters and calendars and proposes filled sessions; the manual cross-checking in Excel goes away.
lenses.autonomous: A certificate expiring in 60 days triggers a proposed slot to the employee and their supervisor without a reminder from L&D.
lenses.ambitious: Nobody works with an expired forklift or VCA certificate, flex workers included, with proof per site for audits.
lenses.joy: No more phone tag with supervisors and rebooking no-shows; L&D keeps the trainer and provider relationships.
lenses.options: Three schedule scenarios per quarter: fewer large sessions, more small shift-aligned sessions, or a mix with external trainers.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets scheduling rules (minimum group size, shift blackout windows, lead times) and checks fill rates and the expiry gap.
reach: Roster coordination for training days with site supervisors
Flex worker certificate checks now done by HR Administrators

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with site managers in peak season about releasing people, and judging which trainer suits which group.
tasks.pattern_why: Constraints are structured (dates, rooms, trainers, shifts, expiries) and the output is a schedule you can check; a rules engine or solver does it without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly job finds certificates expiring within 60 days or new enrolments without a session.
steps: Read expiries from Studytube and employee site and shift data from AFAS
Read room and trainer availability from Outlook resource calendars
Propose sessions and attendee lists that fit rosters
On approval book in Studytube and send Teams/Outlook invites
Flag no-shows and conflicts for rebooking
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves new sessions and handles conflicts the rules cannot solve.
data_needed: Trainer availability and provider lead times
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube session records plus a SharePoint schedule log

evidence.claim: LMS platforms support session scheduling and automatic enrolment from expiry rules
Microsoft Bookings and resource mailboxes handle room and trainer availability

risks: Shift roster data is not in AFAS or lags behind real rosters
Flex workers from agencies are missing from Studytube
Automated invites ignored on the warehouse floor without a supervisor nudge
research_questions: Where do current shift rosters live per site, and can they be read automatically?
Does the Studytube API expose certificate expiries and session booking?
How many hours per month go to rebooking today?
Are flex workers' certificates tracked in Studytube or only at the agency?

tasks.short: Track training spend against budget and explain it to the HR and Finance Directors each quarter.

today.trigger: Month close and the quarterly budget review with Finance.
steps: Export training invoices and cost lines from AFAS general ledger and accounts payable
Match invoices to courses and participants from Studytube in Excel
Split costs per site, department and mandatory versus development
Build a budget versus actual report in Excel and PowerPoint
Explain overspend and justify next year's request
drudgery: Matching invoices to courses line by line
Rebuilding the same slides each quarter
today.time_sinks: Invoices with vague descriptions and training costs hidden in agency invoices that must be traced by hand.

lenses.faster: A Power BI page joins AFAS cost lines with Studytube completions; matching invoices by hand disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Each month after close the report refreshes and an LLM drafts a short variance note for review.
lenses.ambitious: Cost per certified employee and per retained hire, so training spend links to 90-day retention and the North Star.
lenses.joy: No invoice matching in Excel; time goes to the conversation about what training is worth.
lenses.options: Budget scenarios for next year: flex volume high or low, in-house versus external trainers, with or without sector training fund subsidies.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the cost-coding rules and dashboard definitions and checks the monthly numbers.
reach: Invoice coding of training costs now done by Bookkeepers
Training budget lines in FP&A forecasts

tasks.human_edge: Arguing the value of a programme with the HR and Finance Directors and deciding what to cut.
tasks.pattern_why: The joins and totals are deterministic; an LLM step codes messy invoice descriptions to courses and drafts the variance text, both checkable.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS month close completed and nightly Power BI refresh.
steps: Pull training cost lines from AFAS and completions from Studytube
LLM codes uncoded invoice lines to course and site, with confidence
Power BI shows budget versus actual, cost per participant and per certificate
LLM drafts a variance note; specialist edits and sends
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves low-confidence coding and the variance note before it goes to Finance.
data_needed: Training cost ledger accounts and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset history and a SharePoint folder with signed-off monthly notes

evidence.claim: Power BI can combine AFAS and LMS extracts in one report
LLMs classify invoice lines to categories with reviewable confidence

risks: Training costs booked on generic accounts, so the base data is unreliable
Training paid via agencies hidden in flex invoices
Numbers drift from Finance reporting if definitions differ
research_questions: Which AFAS ledger accounts and cost centres carry training costs today, and how clean are they?
What share of training spend arrives via agency invoices?
Does the Controller accept an L&D-owned Power BI page as the source for budget reviews?

tasks.short: Build a programme that grows team leaders and planners from warehouse and transport staff.

today.trigger: Annual talent review, or a shortage of shift leaders and planners.
steps: Collect nominations from site managers and HR Business Partners
Design the programme modules, mentoring and assignments
Find providers or internal trainers and set up Studytube
Run kick-off and follow participants over months
Report progress and promotions to the HR Director
drudgery: Writing module material and slides from scratch
Chasing participants and mentors for progress updates
today.time_sinks: Content creation and follow-up with participants across three sites and shifts.

lenses.faster: AI drafts module outlines, case exercises from real warehouse situations and participant materials in Dutch and other floor languages.
lenses.autonomous: Progress nudges and reflection prompts go to participants after each module without L&D chasing.
lenses.ambitious: Every site has a visible path from order picker to shift leader, open to flex workers who stay, with internal promotion rates tracked.
lenses.joy: Less slide-building; more time coaching participants and their mentors.
lenses.options: Several programme designs (short modular, cohort year, on-the-job rotation) with cost and impact estimates for the HR Director.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the talent pipeline and selection criteria and checks that it is fair across sites and groups.
reach: Succession planning input usually done by HR Business Partners
Leadership practice scenarios for new team leaders

tasks.human_edge: Spotting potential, building trust with nominees and managers, and fair selection the works council can see.
tasks.pattern_why: Design and selection stay with the person; AI speeds drafting, options and practice material.

in_practice.trigger: Programme design cycle or a new cohort.
steps: Specialist sets goals and target roles
AI drafts programme options, module content and role-play cases
Specialist tests with site managers and adjusts
Materials load into Studytube; automated progress prompts go out
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director decide programme design and selection; no AI ranking of candidates.
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube programme records and SharePoint programme folder

evidence.claim: LLM assistants draft training content, cases and role-plays
AI role-play practice for managers is offered commercially

risks: Using AI to select or rank candidates is high-risk under the EU AI Act and needs works council consent (WOR art. 27)
Generic content that does not fit warehouse reality
research_questions: How many shift leader and planner roles were filled internally in the last two years?
Would site managers release people for a cohort programme in peak season?
Does the works council need to approve the selection approach?

tasks.short: Create training on energy saving, packaging waste and fuel-efficient driving for drivers and warehouse staff.

today.trigger: Sustainability targets, CSRD reporting needs, or a customer requirement.
steps: Gather input from facilities, fleet and the sustainability lead
Write content and toolbox talks
Build e-learning in Studytube
Roll out per site and track completions
today.time_sinks: Writing and translating content for a low-frequency topic with little existing material.

lenses.faster: AI turns policies and fuel or waste data into toolbox talks, short e-learning and quizzes in several languages.
lenses.autonomous: Completions flow to the dashboard; refreshers trigger when a site's waste or fuel figures slip.
lenses.ambitious: Every driver gets eco-driving feedback tied to telematics, done properly for the first time.
lenses.joy: Less searching for material; more time on the floor seeing what changes.
lenses.options: Several formats per topic: 10-minute toolbox talk, micro-learning, poster, video script.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets learning goals and checks whether behaviour and figures change.
reach: Sustainability training evidence for CSRD reporting
Toolbox talk content for site safety coordinators

tasks.human_edge: Making the message credible for drivers and pickers and getting supervisors to lead it.
tasks.pattern_why: Low-volume, content-heavy work where the person leads and AI drafts.

in_practice.trigger: New sustainability target or yearly training plan.
steps: Specialist gives AI the policy, data and audience
AI drafts toolbox talks, e-learning and quizzes in Dutch, Polish and English
Specialist checks with fleet or facilities experts
Publish in Studytube and track completions
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and subject expert approve content before publishing.
data_needed: Fuel and waste figures per site
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube course versions and SharePoint content folder

evidence.claim: LLM assistants draft and translate training content and quizzes

risks: Individual telematics feedback needs works council consent and an AVG check
research_questions: Which customers or regulations actually ask for sustainability training evidence?
Is fleet telematics data available and allowed for personal feedback?
Which languages are used on each site?

role.altitude: From planning sessions and writing courses to running the skills system: rules for certificate compliance, cost coding and programme design, and checking that training moves 90-day retention and internal promotion.
reach: Certificate compliance checks for flex workers (HR Administrator)
Training cost coding and forecasts (Bookkeeper, FP&A Analyst)
Week-one onboarding learning paths (Recruiter, HR Business Partner)
Succession and internal mobility input (HR Business Partner)
Training dashboards (People Analytics and HRIS Analyst)
role.ceiling_note: About 220 of roughly 1,600 hours per FTE sit in these four tasks; scheduling and cost reporting can drop by about two thirds, but programme design, coaching and site negotiation stay human. The limits are data quality in AFAS, Studytube and shift rosters, plus works council consent for anything that judges people.
skills_to_grow: Power BI and data modelling on AFAS and Studytube
Power Automate and LMS API workflows
Prompting and reviewing AI-drafted learning content
EU AI Act, AVG and WOR basics for HR tools
role.ambitious_version: L&D runs a live skills and certificate picture for all 1,200 employees and the flex pool, schedules itself, ties every euro to certificates, promotions and 90-day retention, and spends the freed time growing shift leaders from the floor.
